title: Bank Feed Setup
subtitle: Adds the bank feed to your tracker: Import Rules, Connections, the review workflow, the split panel, student loans kept separate from household debt, a copy-for-AI financial snapshot, and the Plaid connection for all your accounts.
intro: Sixteen script files change or are new; `Helpers.gs` does not change. After pasting, you run **Upgrade workbook** once: it adds the new tabs and columns to your live Sheet and keeps every row you have entered. Nothing is deleted.

Then you give the script your two Plaid keys (in the script's private settings, never in a cell), set the start date for history, and connect each bank from the **Bank feed** menu. Each bank uses one of the 10 free Plaid slots for good, so the page is careful about duplicates.

**What does not change:** your transactions, paychecks, accounts, debts, funds, budgets, reviews, the Dashboard month you selected, and your settings. Two headers are renamed to make room for student loans: *Reviewed Debt Balance* → *Reviewed Household Debt* (Monthly Summary) and *Total Debt Balance* → *Household Debt Balance* (Monthly Review).
**Privacy:** Plaid keys go into Script Properties only. Never paste them into chat, email or GitHub.

steps.text: Open the Household Finance Tracker Sheet. Choose **File → Version history → Name current version**, type `Before bank feed`, and click **Save**.
steps.note: If anything looks wrong afterwards, File → Version history → See version history lets you go back to this one.

steps.text: Choose **Extensions → Apps Script**. Click **Code.gs** (your Config file). Click inside the code, press {{Ctrl}}+{{A}}, then {{Delete}}, and paste.
steps.note: This file carries the whole schema change. Paste it first. (You can rename Code.gs to Config via its ⋮ menu if you like; it changes nothing.)

steps.text: Click **Reference.gs**. Select all, delete, and paste.
Click **Tables.gs**. Select all, delete, and paste.
Click **Dashboard.gs**. Select all, delete, and paste.
Click **SampleData.gs**. Select all, delete, and paste.
Click **QA.gs**. Select all, delete, and paste.
Click **Main.gs**. Select all, delete, and paste.
Click **Api.gs**. Select all, delete, and paste.
steps.note: Helpers.gs is unchanged; leave it alone.

steps.text: Click the **+** next to Files, choose **Script**, name it `Import`, press {{Enter}}, and paste into the new file (select all and delete the two default lines first).
steps.note: Google adds ".gs" itself.

steps.text: Click **+ → Script**, name it `Plaid`, select all, delete, and paste.
Click **+ → Script**, name it `Upgrade`, select all, delete, and paste.
Click **+ → HTML** (not Script), name it `SplitPanel`, select all, delete, and paste.
steps.note: The three HTML files are the side panel and the two dialogs. They must be HTML files with exactly these names.

steps.text: Click **+ → HTML**, name it `RuleDialog`, select all, delete, and paste.
Click **+ → HTML**, name it `ConnectDialog`, select all, delete, and paste.
Click **+ → Script**, name it `Export`, select all, delete, and paste.
steps.note: This is the Copy financial snapshot for AI feature.

steps.text: Click **+ → HTML**, name it `ExportDialog`, select all, delete, paste, and save everything with {{Ctrl}}+{{S}}.
steps.note: The file list should now show Code (Config), Helpers, Reference, Tables, Dashboard, SampleData, QA, Main, Api, Import, Plaid, Upgrade, Export, SplitPanel.html, RuleDialog.html, ConnectDialog.html, ExportDialog.html — 17 files.

steps.text: Click **Upgrade.gs**, choose **upgradeWorkbook** in the function dropdown, and click **Run**. Approve the permission prompt if one appears (the new code reaches out to Plaid and manages a daily trigger, so Google asks again).
steps.note: The Execution log ends with a short report: Added tab: Import Rules, Added tab: Connections, the columns added to Accounts, Import Staging, Debts, Quarterly Debt Review, Monthly Summary and Monthly Review, and the lists added. Takes well under a minute.

steps.text: Go back to the Sheet and reload it. Two new tabs sit between Import Staging and Change Log: **Import Rules** and **Connections**. The Finance Tracker menu now starts with *Import reviewed rows*, *Split the selected row…*, *Make a rule from the selected row…* and has a **Bank feed** submenu.
steps.note: Your rows are all still there. Dashboard B3 still shows the month you had selected.

steps.text: Open **Debts**. The KPI band now reads Household Debt (excl. student loans) · Student Loans · All Debt · Estimated Monthly Interest · Total Minimum Payments · Current Quarter Ends, and there is a new last column **Debt Group**. For each real debt you enter, set Debt Group to **Student Loans** or **Household**; the sample student loan is already Student Loans.
steps.note: Monthly Summary's debt column is now household-only, with a separate Student Loan Balance column at the far right. Net worth still counts everything.

steps.text: Run **Finance Tracker → Run QA checks**. Expect PASS throughout; the new lines cover Import Staging, Import Rules and Connections.
steps.note: If anything says FAIL, send me the line.

steps.text: Try **Finance Tracker → Copy financial snapshot for AI…**. A window builds a plain-text briefing (income, cash flow, spending by category, funds, debts with student loans separate, accounts and net worth, recurring bills, credit scores, data-quality notes). Click **Copy snapshot**, open a Claude project, paste, and ask it something.
steps.note: It is built from the raw tables each time you open it. While sample data is present the first line says so.

sections.heading: Give the script your Plaid keys

steps.text: In a new browser tab open [dashboard.plaid.com](https://dashboard.plaid.com) and sign in. In the left sidebar choose **Developers → Keys**. You need two values: **client_id** and the **Production** secret (the free Trial runs against Production; do not use the Sandbox secret).
steps.note: Keep this tab open; you will copy from it twice. Do not paste these values anywhere except where the next step says.

steps.text: Back in the Apps Script editor, click the gear icon **Project Settings** (left sidebar). Scroll to **Script Properties** and click **Add script property**. Property: `PLAID_CLIENT_ID`, Value: your client_id. Click **Add script property** again: Property `PLAID_SECRET`, Value: the Production secret. Click **Save script properties**.
steps.note: Spelling matters: capital letters and underscores exactly as shown. These two boxes are the only place the keys ever live.

steps.text: Return to the Sheet. Choose **Finance Tracker → Bank feed → Status**. It should say PLAID_CLIENT_ID: set, PLAID_SECRET: set, 0 of 10 connections.
steps.note: It shows whether each key is set, never the key itself. "missing" means a property name is misspelled.

steps.text: Choose **Bank feed → Set history start date…** and enter the first day you want imported, as yyyy-mm-dd (for example the first of this month). Transactions before that day are ignored, and the date also decides how much history Plaid is asked for when you connect.
steps.note: Set this before connecting the first bank. It can be moved later, but Plaid only fetches history back to the date in force when a bank is connected.

steps.text: Choose **Bank feed → Connect a bank…**. Leave **Spending account** selected and click **Continue**, then click **Open Plaid to connect your bank**. A Plaid page opens in a new tab: search `Independent Bank`, pick the Michigan one, sign in with your bank login, and select all three accounts (checking, savings, credit card). When Plaid says you are done, close that tab.
steps.note: Do this at home or on cellular, not on public Wi-Fi. Plaid never shows us your bank password.

steps.text: Back in the dialog click **I've finished in Plaid**. Step 3 lists the three accounts Plaid found. For each one pick the matching row: Checking → ACC-007, Savings → ACC-008, Credit Card → ACC-009. Leave **Import transactions** ticked for all three. Click **Save and run the first sync**.
steps.note: If the dialog says "not finished yet", finish the steps in Plaid's tab and click again. If a bank account does not match any row, choose Create a new Accounts row.

steps.text: When it finishes, the dialog reports how many transactions landed in Import Staging and that balances were updated. Open **Connections**: CONN-001 Independent Bank, Status Active, Last Sync just now. Open **Accounts**: ACC-007/008/009 now show External Account ID, Connection ID and a fresh Current Balance.
steps.note: A long Last Error on Connections means something to tell me about; copy its text.

steps.text: Repeat **Connect a bank…** as a **Spending account** for Capital One (→ ACC-010), PayPal (→ ACC-006), **American Express** (Create a new Accounts row) and **Venmo** (Create a new Accounts row). Capital One and Amex will bounce you to their own login pages inside Plaid; that is expected.
steps.note: Connect each bank once. If a connection fails halfway, use Bank feed → Repair a connection…, never Connect again for the same bank: a second connection would use another slot for good.

steps.text: Repeat **Connect a bank…** as **Investment, retirement or HSA account** for Acorns (→ ACC-011), Fidelity (→ ACC-012) and HealthEquity (→ ACC-013). Leave **Import transactions** unticked for these; they update balances only.
steps.note: If Fidelity shows a "request access" message inside Plaid, approve it and try again in a day. Bank feed → Status should end at 9 of 10 connections.

steps.text: Choose **Bank feed → Turn nightly sync on**. From now on the feed runs every morning around 5 AM; **Bank feed → Sync now** runs it any time.
steps.note: Google may ask for permission to run on a schedule. Approve it.

sections.heading: Your weekly review, with real rows

steps.text: Open **Import Staging**. New rows have Status **Needs Review** (red), with Suggested Type / Category / Subcategory / Spending Type empty or pre-filled. Fix or fill those cells with the dropdowns, then tick **Reviewed?** on each row you are happy with.
steps.note: Transfers between your own accounts and credit-card payments are detected and imported automatically (Status Imported, Paired Import ID filled). Turn that off on App Setup if you ever want to see them first.

steps.text: For a bill or merchant that is always the same (the electric company, a subscription, a paycheck), click its row and choose **Finance Tracker → Make a rule from the selected row…**. Check the match text, tick **Always auto-import**, and save. The rule applies to every waiting row that matches and to every future one.
steps.note: For a paycheck, leave the amount out of it (the rule matches the description), choose Type Income and the person, and tick Always auto-import. The deposit links itself to the paycheck in Income when you enter the pay stub.

steps.text: For Meijer, Walmart, Target or Costco, make a rule the same way but tick **Split required** instead of auto-import. Those rows then show Status **Needs Split**: click one and choose **Finance Tracker → Split the selected row…**. The side panel shows the amount; add a line per category until Remaining reads $0.00, then **Save split**.
steps.note: The receipt-photo version of this (AI reads the receipt into the lines for you) is the next phase.

steps.text: Choose **Finance Tracker → Import reviewed rows**. Every ticked row becomes a transaction; rows missing a category are listed with the reason and stay in staging. The Dashboard's top-right note shows how many rows are still waiting.
steps.note: Then check the Dashboard: Spending moved by exactly the rows you imported.
